name: The Headless Horseman

alignment.name: Chaotic Evil
alignment.description:
Chaotic evil creatures have a complete disregard for others. They kill, steal, and betray others to gain power. Their word is meaningless and their actions destructive. Their worldviews can be so warped that they destroy anything and anyone that doesn’t directly contribute to their interests.
	By the standards of good and lawful good people, chaotic evil is as abhorrent as evil, perhaps even more so. Chaotic evil monsters such as demons and orcs are at least as much of a threat to civilization and general well-being as evil monsters are. An evil creature and a chaotic evil creature are both opposed to good, but they don’t have much respect for each other either and rarely cooperate toward common goals.
	For the purpose of game effects, a chaotic evil creature is also considered evil.

languages: Understands all spoken languages; does not speak
description: This is the size of a typical human and serves as a standard in the game. This category has no special rules.

traits.name: Executioner's Step
traits.details: When the Horseman makes a charge attack (whether on foot or mounted), he gains combat advantage against the target of the charge.

traits.name: Combat Advantage
traits.details: The horseman deals ongoing 10 damage (save ends) on a hit against any creature granting him combat advantage.

traits.name: Bound to the Road
traits.details: The Horseman is linked to the road. He treats all terrain beyond the road as difficult terrain, and he cannot move beyond line of sight of the road.

hit.description: damage (crit 4d8+7 damage, and the target is dazed until the end of the Horseman’s next turn). This attack rolls a critical hit on an 18–20
the target is reduced to 0 hit points.

miss.description: 2d8 + 23 damage, and the target is dazed until the end of the Horseman’s next turn

powers.name: Unholy Resilience
powers.trigger: when the Horseman is subject to an immobilizing, restraining, or slowing effect

effect.description: The Horseman makes a saving throw against the triggering effect, even if it does not normally allow a save to end.
